title: Delta Outage Snarls Holiday Flights. Storms Threaten Thanksgiving. Ukraine Says It Sank a Warship.
subject: Delta Outage Snarls Holiday Flights. Storms Threaten Thanksgiving. Ukraine Says It Sank a Warship.
preview_text: Thanksgiving travel snags, the biggest Democratic House majority since 1992 and a planned Iowa Army blast.
description: A Delta system outage delayed flights nationwide, storms threaten both coasts for Thanksgiving, and Ukraine says it sank a Russian warship off Libya.
contents_extra: Why the Army plans to detonate unstable explosives in Iowa, trivia and your poll

stories.title: A Delta System Outage Delays Flights Days Before Thanksgiving

photo.alt: Split-flap style flight board; file photo.

paragraphs: Over 1,000 Delta flights were delayed Sunday after a system that calculates aircraft weight malfunctioned, the AP reports via NBC News. The FAA issued about an hourlong ground stop for some flights into Atlanta. The FAA said the delays were not tied to its systems.

Delta said Sunday the system was fixed, CBS News reports. As of Sunday evening, Delta had canceled 202 flights. Delta said it was rebooking customers and offering refunds to those who no longer wish to travel. Delta also said the outage was not the result of a hack, ABC News reports.

stories.title: Storms on Both Coasts Could Disrupt Thanksgiving Travel

photo.alt: Waves crashing against a lighthouse; file photo.

paragraphs: A storm could bring 50 mph gusts and coastal flooding to the Northeast on Thanksgiving, forecasters said, NBC News reports. New York City warned of gusts of 40 to 45 mph. Macy's parade balloons cannot fly in gusts above 34 mph.

A coastal flood warning covers San Francisco Bay shorelines from Monday morning through Thursday afternoon, ABC News reports. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie urged residents to consider not traveling for the holiday. Rain is expected to sweep across Northern California on Wednesday.

stories.title: Ukraine Says Its Naval Drones Sank a Russian Warship Off Libya

photo.alt: Navy aircraft carrier in a fjord; file photo.

paragraphs: Zelenskyy said Monday that seven Ukrainian naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury, NBC News reports. Ukraine's Security Service said the attack happened near the Libyan port of Benghazi. That is some 1,500 miles from the front lines, it said.

Zelenskyy said a Russian cargo ship, the Angara, was also hit, ABC News reports. He said a Russian Ka-27 helicopter was destroyed too. Zelenskyy said Moscow used the Angara to transport weapons, CBS News reports.

stories.title: Democrats Clinch Their Largest House Majority Since 1992

photo.alt: Dome of the U.S. Capitol; file photo.

paragraphs: Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated GOP Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, NBC News projects. NBC News projects Democrats will hold at least 258 House seats. That would be the largest Democratic majority since 1992, NBC News reports.

Hubbard won a recount after leading Foxx 48.7% to 48.6% with 99% of the estimated vote reported, ABC News reports. Hubbard said Foxx called him Sunday to concede, CBS News reports. Foxx has represented the state in the House since 2005.

deep_dive.title: Why the Army Plans to Blow Up Unstable Explosives in Iowa

photo.alt: Danger keep out sign on a fence; file photo.

paragraphs: What happened. The Army said Sunday it will carry out a controlled detonation at an Iowa plant on Wednesday, the AP reports via NBC News. The site holds several tons of lead azide, a bomb-making chemical. The Army invoked emergency provisions to get around a court order that had paused the plan.

Why it matters. Officials say the chemicals are unstable and could explode on their own as temperatures drop. The government warned temperatures were expected to fall below 30 degrees, CBS News reports. Critics worry about toxic lead dust spreading across parts of Iowa and Illinois, CBS News reports. Experts say no level of lead exposure is safe, Al Jazeera reports.

What each side says. The Army says a controlled blast is far safer than an uncontrolled explosion, according to its court filing. Earthjustice lawyer Thien Chau said anyone can claim an emergency at any point, Al Jazeera reports. Environmental groups said the emergency is of the Army's own making. They filed a new motion Sunday seeking to block the detonation, CBS News reports.

What comes next. The Army set Wednesday to allow optimal weather conditions and mitigation measures, it said. Residents were told to stay inside and keep windows and doors closed, NBC News reports. They were also told to bring pets and livestock indoors. Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds said Sunday that state agencies are preparing for the detonation.

World view: COP31 ends without a deal. The climate summit in Turkey collapsed Sunday over fossil fuels, and U.N. chief Antonio Guterres said he was deeply disappointed; CBS News reports.
Russian strikes kill at least 15 near Kyiv. Rescuers searched for residents trapped under a partially collapsed apartment block; Al Jazeera reports.
Saudi Arabia reports a drone headed for Riyadh. It said it intercepted a Houthi drone, while Bahrain said an Iranian attack injured two people; CNBC reports.
Attacks on West Bank medics surge. Physicians for Human Rights Israel documented a 350% rise in incidents involving Palestinian health workers from 2022 to 2024; Al Jazeera reports.
Need to know: Three are killed at an Ohio baby shower. Police in Parma said one person was also wounded Saturday in an apparent domestic dispute; the AP reports via NBC News.
An Amtrak train derails in Louisiana. The train hit an 18-wheeler east of Lafayette on Sunday, and Amtrak said all passenger cars stayed upright; ABC News reports.
A gas pipeline fire lights up Alabama. The operator said nobody was hurt and the cause of the Saturday night fire is under investigation; CBS News reports.
Bessent says the U.S. needs answers from Nvidia. The Treasury secretary spoke Sunday as questions swirl over whether the chipmaker complied with export limits; CBS News reports.
Money & markets: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler. The all-stock deal values Zscaler at about $43.9 billion, and Zscaler shares jumped in premarket trading Monday; CNBC reports.
Treasury yields rise early Monday. The 10-year yield was up 4 basis points to 4.959% as stock futures pointed to a rebound; CNBC reports.
Home sales hit a 16-year low. Closed sales of existing homes fell in October as mortgage rates spiked; CNBC reports.
Social Security checks rise in January. A 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment takes effect, though higher Medicare premiums could eat into it; CNBC reports.
Future frontiers: Groups urge Amazon and eBay to drop AI toys. More than 155 child safety groups and experts made the call, and Amazon said it removed some tested toys; NBC News reports.
A Meta executive warns about superintelligence. Chief AI officer Alexandr Wang said Sunday that AI far beyond human intellect is imminent; Al Jazeera reports.
AI data centers draw infrastructure money. Preqin data shows $62 billion was raised across 21 infrastructure funds in the third quarter; CNBC reports.
A robot startup drops worker health coverage. Foundation employees were told coverage ended retroactively to October, according to a memo obtained by CNBC; CNBC reports.
The score: The 49ers rout the Vikings in Mexico City. San Francisco won 35-10 on Sunday night to move to 9-1; ESPN reports.
Tarik Skubal agrees to a record Mets deal. The pitcher agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract, sources told ESPN; ESPN reports.
Detroit trades Dylan Larkin to Montreal. The former Red Wings captain moved to the Canadiens in a blockbuster deal on Sunday; ESPN reports.
Broadcaster Tom Jackson dies at 75. The former Broncos star was a mainstay of ESPN Sunday football shows for three decades; CBS News reports.
Life & culture: The Hunger Games roars back. Sunrise on the Reaping debuted with $120 million in North American theaters, according to studio estimates; the AP reports via NBC News.
Miley Cyrus marries Maxx Morando. The singer wed the rock drummer in Palm Springs, according to a post on her Instagram account; the AP reports via NBC News.
A Don Toliver concert is evacuated. About 12,000 people left a Manchester arena after a substance believed to be tear gas was released; NBC News reports.
A Florida town cancels its Christmas parade. Deltona blamed a voter-approved property tax overhaul, its city manager said Saturday; NBC News reports.

trivia.question: On which day does the Army plan to carry out the Iowa detonation?
trivia.explanation: C. Wednesday. The Army said it plans the detonation on Wednesday to allow for optimal weather conditions, CBS News reports.

poll.question: Has bad weather or a flight delay ever changed your Thanksgiving plans?
